months.note: 번식기는 3월부터 6월 중순까지이며, 알은 3월 하순~4월에 낳는다. 겨울에는 전국의 해안·하구·저수지·농경지 같은 트인 곳에서도 보인다.

summary: 외딴 섬과 해안 절벽에서 번식하는 대형 매류로, 천연기념물이자 멸종위기 야생생물 Ⅱ급이다. 절벽이나 높은 나무 위에서 지켜보다가 날아가는 새를 발견하면 높은 곳에서 빠르게 내리꽂아 공중에서 잡는다. 오리·도요새 같은 중형 조류를 주로 먹고, 번식기에는 수컷이 공중에서 암컷에게 먹이를 건네는 모습을 볼 수 있다.

sexes.text: 암수 거의 같은 색이다. 암컷이 수컷보다 훨씬 커서(수컷 약 38cm, 암컷 약 51cm) 크기 차이로 짐작할 수 있다.

young: 등이 갈색이고, 연한 황갈색 아랫면에 굵은 흑갈색 세로줄무늬가 가득하다.

similar.how: 더 작고 날개가 가늘며, 아랫면에 가로줄 대신 굵은 검은 세로줄이 있다. 허벅지와 아래꼬리덮깃이 무늬 없는 적갈색이다.
훨씬 가볍고 작으며, 등이 적갈색이고 꼬리가 길다. 공중에서 정지비행을 하며 먹이를 찾는다.

art.subject: Peregrine Falcon (Falco peregrinus), adult, as seen on Korean island cliffs and coasts: crown, nape and face slate-black forming a hood, with a broad, wedge-shaped black moustachial patch below the eye; throat and lower cheeks white, sharply set off from the black. Back, scapulars and upperwing dark blue-grey with faint darker barring, paler blue-grey on the rump; wingtips blackish. Tail blue-grey with narrow dark bars and a thin whitish tip. Upper breast white or pale buff with few small spots; lower breast, belly, flanks and thighs white to pale buff, densely crossed with fine black bars. Eye dark brown with a yellow eye-ring; cere yellow; bill bluish-grey with a black tip; feet bright yellow with black talons.
art.pose: perched upright on a rocky sea-cliff ledge, body erect, head turned scanning the sea
art.scene: a rugged rocky sea cliff on an uninhabited island off Korea's southwest coast in early spring, waves breaking white below, a few seabirds over the water, sparse pines and grass on the cliff top; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, in flight seen from above: dark blue-grey back and upperwing with paler blue-grey rump, blackish head, black wingtips, barred tail with pale tip, long pointed broad-based wings
adult, in flight seen from below: black hood and broad moustache against a white throat, densely fine-barred pale underparts and underwing, long pointed wings, yellow feet tucked under the tail
adult stooping, seen from the side and slightly above: wings half-folded close to the body, compact teardrop shape, black hood and moustache, yellow feet tucked
art.build: Large, powerful falcon, 34–50cm; the female is much larger than the male, nearly crow-sized and far bulkier than a Common Kestrel. Broad chest, large head, strong hooked bill. Wings long, pointed and broad-based; at rest the wingtips nearly reach the tail tip. Tail fairly short, slightly tapered. In flight a compact anchor shape with stiff, shallow wingbeats; stoops at great speed with the wings folded close to the body. Perches upright on cliff ledges and high snags.
avoid: Do not streak the underparts lengthwise (Hobby, or juvenile Peregrine); the adult is finely barred across.
Do not paint rufous thighs or vent (Hobby) or a rufous back (Kestrel).
Do not paint a thin pencil-line moustache; the Peregrine's is broad and wedge-shaped.
Do not paint a long tail; the tail is fairly short and the wingtips nearly reach its tip.
